kept.claim: Switching error-invalid-multivalued-size from i18next `{{0}}` placeholders to Java MessageFormat `{0}` / `{2,choice,...}` in the account-ui and admin-ui bundles makes the React UIs render the raw placeholders and choice syntax to users.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] MessageFormat syntax in i18next-consumed bundle renders literally in Account/Admin UI

**Severity:** HIGH — user-facing validation error shows `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` verbatim.

### The Problem

```properties
-error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).
+error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.
```

The same change is made in `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties:3138`.

### Theory / Proof

- These bundles are served raw by `ThemeResource` (`services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/ThemeResource.java:141-154`, values are copied straight from `theTheme.getMessages(...)`, no format conversion).
- The account UI (`js/apps/account-ui/src/i18n.ts`) and admin UI (`js/apps/admin-ui/src/i18n/i18n.ts`) feed them into i18next with default interpolation, whose placeholder syntax is `{{name}}`. i18next has no support for ICU/MessageFormat `{n,choice,...}`.
- The error comes from `MultiValueValidator.MESSAGE_INVALID_SIZE` and is rendered by `setUserProfileServerError` in `js/libs/ui-shared/src/user-profile/utils.ts:70-85`, which calls `t(key, {0: ..., 1: ..., 2: ...})`. With `{{0}}` this interpolated correctly; with `{0}` nothing is substituted.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Before: "Attribute email must have at least 1 and at most 2 value(s)." After this PR: "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}." in both the account console and admin console. The login theme (Freemarker + `MessageFormat`) is fine; only the React consumers break. It looks like the change was done to make the verifier happy (the verifier special-cases this key in `normalizeValue`), but the root cause was only `(s)`-style text; the `{{n}}` placeholders were correct for these two bundles.

### Research

i18next interpolation docs: default `prefix`/`suffix` are `{{` / `}}`; plurals use `_one`/`_other` suffix keys, not ICU `choice`. Other keys in the same account-ui bundle use `{{0}}` consistently.

### Recommendation

Revert the two React bundles to i18next syntax (and keep MessageFormat only in the Freemarker login/admin base theme):

```properties
error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).
```

or, if pluralization is wanted, use i18next plural keys (`..._one` / `..._other` with `count`).
kept.evidence: ThemeResource.getLocalizationTexts returns raw values; DefaultThemeManager only does ${env} replacement; account-ui/src/i18n.ts and admin-ui/src/i18n/i18n.ts use default i18next {{ }} interpolation with no ICU/postProcessor; MultiValueValidator.java:46/137 emits the key and ui-shared/src/user-profile/utils.ts:64-88 calls t() with 0/1/2 params; keycloak.v3/account and keycloak.v2/admin bundles override base, so the changed string is served and renders literally. Base-theme changes (Freemarker/MessageFormat) are correct.

dropped.claim: The anchor-mismatch error omits the file and key (the `key` parameter is unused), so a build failure aggregated across hundreds of message files cannot be traced to its source.
dropped.body:
## [ISSUE] Anchor mismatch error has no file or key

**Severity:** MEDIUM — build fails with a message a translator cannot act on.

### The Problem

```java
messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string");
```

`santizeAnchors(String key, ...)` receives `key` but never uses it, and `file` is not included either. Compare with the other two messages in this class, which both include the file (`"Illegal HTML in key " + key + " for file " + file`, `"Duplicate keys in file '" + file.getAbsolutePath()`).

### Theory / Proof

`ThemeVerifierMojo.execute()` iterates every `messages_*.properties` in every resource directory and throws `new MojoFailureException("Validation errors: " + messages)`. With ~40 locales x several themes, `<a href="{0}">` appears in many files and keys, so "Didn't find anchor tag <a href=\"{0}\"> in original string" is ambiguous.

### What happens today vs. what will break

The current tree passes, so nothing is shown. The next community translation that adds or alters a link (the main purpose of this check) fails the build with no pointer to the file/key.

### Recommendation

```java
messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string for key " + key + " in file " + file);
```

and assert on the key in `verifyNoChangedAnchors`.
dropped.evidence: VerifyMessageProperties.java:150-161 breaks without removing the unmatched <a> tag; neither policy (lines 58-63) allows <a>, so line 111 always adds 'Illegal HTML in key <key> for file <file>' for the same key immediately after, giving file/key context in the aggregated MojoFailureException.

dropped.claim: Path heuristics are applied to the absolute path, so a checkout whose path contains "email" silently relaxes the check for every file, and one containing "resources-community" breaks the English-file lookup.
dropped.body:
## [ISSUE] Path heuristics run against the absolute path, not the theme-relative path

**Severity:** LOW — environment-dependent behaviour of a security check.

### The Problem

```java
if (file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")) {
    value = value.replaceAll(Pattern.quote(" style=\"direction: rtl;\""), "");
}
```
and line 74:
```java
String englishFile = file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")
```

### Theory / Proof

`getAbsolutePath()` includes the user's workspace path. If Keycloak is cloned under e.g. `/home/ci/email-service/keycloak`, every login/account/admin file gets the email-only relaxation (a `style="direction: rtl;"` attribute becomes accepted anywhere). `replaceAll` on the whole path also rewrites any parent directory named `...resources-community...`, pointing to a non-existent English file; that surfaces as an unchecked `RuntimeException` (lines 70/79) rather than a `MojoExecutionException`.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Works for normal checkouts. Breaks/relaxes only for particular workspace names, which makes it hard to diagnose.

### Recommendation

Match on path segments instead:

```java
Path p = file.toPath();
boolean isEmail = p.getParent() != null && p.getParent().getParent() != null
        && p.getParent().getParent().getFileName().toString().equals("email");
```
and resolve the English sibling via `file.toPath().resolveSibling("messages_en.properties")` with only the `resources-community` segment swapped; throw `MojoExecutionException` on IO failure.
dropped.evidence: The only ' style="direction: rtl;"' occurrence is in base/email/messages_ar.properties, so a path containing 'email' changes no result; a parent directory named 'resources-community' is a contrived environment, and the RuntimeException at line 79 still fails loudly with the path.

The duplicate-key test was also relaxed from `contains` to `hasItem`, so extra unexpected messages are no longer detected. The trickiest parts of the change (entity unescaping, `` removal after `{{`, `
` normalization, the matching-anchor removal path) have no test showing they yield an empty list. ### Recommendation Add a fixture pair, e.g. `validHtml_en.properties` / `validHtml_de.properties`: ```properties key=Some bold and link & {{name}}
``` ```java @Test void verifyValidHtmlAccepted() throws MojoExecutionException { MatcherAssert.assertThat(getFile("validHtml_de.properties").verify(), Matchers.empty()); } ``` and restore `Matchers.contains(...)` in the duplicate-key test.
